technical.summary: Short-term momentum is bullish with strong candlestick and trend-following confirmation, but overbought conditions, weak intermediate moving average alignment, and negative volume signals limit conviction for a high-probability swing entry.

fundamental.summary: AFL shows no insider buying, no institutional accumulation, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and earnings in 68 days—insufficient smart money conviction to support a trade.

sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (10/100) presents contrarian buy opportunity, but mixed congressional activity (1 small purchase vs 1 small sale, oldest trade 411 days old) and absent news sentiment provide no confirmation.

risk.summary: Extreme VIX crisis regime (378.4) combined with flat yield curve and negative macro score (-3) creates severely unfavourable conditions; 68-day earnings window adds moderate event risk.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term momentum is genuinely bullish (three white soldiers, supertrend, RSI, hull) with price near support (51.56), offering a contrarian fear-zone entry with defined risk.
debate.key_bear_argument: Overbought oscillators, price below all major moving averages (50/200 EMA/SMA), negative volume (CMF, OBV), zero fundamental conviction, extreme VIX crisis regime, and no triggered strategies create a high-probability mean-reversion trap rather than a swing entry.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term momentum (three white soldiers, supertrend, RSI) is genuinely bullish at support, but this is contradicted by overbought oscillators, price below all major moving averages, and negative volume—classic mean-reversion trap setup.
